analysis.title: The 720: SK Hynix, StanChart, Coupang, Hitachi, DISCO, NEC, SEMCO, Elite Material, Songfa, Alphabet & Microsoft, FOMC
key_insights: SK Hynix reported a 3Q26 operating profit beat on stronger-than-expected DRAM, NAND and HBM pricing. GS reiterates Buy and a W3.5mn 12m TP and raises 2027E-2028E EPS by 19-22%, citing conventional DRAM pricing and volume and management's W100tn 2026 shareholder return plan.
SK Hynix management says HBM4 mass production is ramping smoothly with yields above targets. Long-term agreements indicate DRAM and HBM are effectively sold out through 2029.

October FOMC left the funds rate unchanged, consistent with a compromise to hike every other meeting. GS expects a second and final hike in December, leaving the funds rate at 4-4.25%, with a third hike in March possible if inflation comes in higher than expected.

Chairman Warsh gave balanced comments: economy and labor market remain strong, inflation expectations are moving in the right direction, and recent tightening is taking effect. Policy task forces report by year-end for a 2027Q1 review, and some future meetings will cover broad monetary strategy without federal funds rate votes.

Coupang: GS lowers 12m TP to US$28 from US$29 and cuts the 2027E Product Commerce adjusted EBITDA margin estimate to 8.7% from 9.6% on a more gradual fixed-cost operating leverage recovery. Channel checks show churned users returning for delivery, but spending still lags historical levels. GS still expects a V-shaped 2027 profit recovery and sees limited structural impact from regulatory scrutiny.

Taiwan ODM/Brands: GS stays positive on the AI server and PC supply chain, citing AI server rack ramps, ASIC server penetration and new smartphone models. Buy-rated: Hon Hai, Wiwynn, Wistron. Neutral: Quanta, Inventec, Compal, ASUS. Sell-rated Pegatron TP cut to NT$73.3 while 2026-28E net income rises 4-6% and revenues 16-28%.
Taiwan supply chain revenues are expected to be flat sequentially but up 44-68% y/y in coming months. GS raises Inventec 2026-28E net income by 6-14%.

Australia Banks: GS launches a NIM dashboard and projects sector NIMs peak and plateau over 1H27, then decline in 2H27. For 2H26 it forecasts NIM +1bp to 1.54% for ANZ, -1bp to 1.88% for Westpac and -2bps to 1.79% for NAB.

DISCO: Buy and 12m TP of ¥105,000 reiterated. GS expects FY3/28 operating profit to beat consensus by more than 20% on CPO equipment demand, OSAT advanced packaging, EMIB-T and hybrid bonding. GS argues fewer HBM layers means more HBM cubes for the same bit demand, which raises back-end processing volume, and sees minimal capacity constraint risk.

NEC: 2Q operating profit missed on restructuring costs, but underlying profit beat consensus by about ¥10bn. Full-year non-GAAP OP guidance rose to ¥460bn from ¥430bn. Underlying non-GAAP OP excluding one-offs grew 30% y/y on domestic IT services mix and submarine cable growth. Buy, 12m TP ¥6,300.

Taiwan CCL: Buy on Elite Material and Taiwan Union Technology with TPs raised to NT$11,700 and NT$3,460. 2026-28 net income estimates rise 13-22% for EMC and 12-27% for TUC on 5-20% near-term price hikes and M8/M9 migration. EMC says supply will stay short of secured LTA volumes even at 15.25mn sheets/month capacity by 2030.

Hon Precision: Buy, TP raised to NT$12,600 after 3Q26 EPS of NT$37.33, 8% above consensus. Management targets 50% capacity expansion in 2027 and a gross margin uplift in 2H27 from Mega Tray mix and CPO Insertion 4 tools in mass production in the first quarter.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics: 3Q26 OP beat on high-value MLCC and FC-BGA mix. Buy, TP raised to W2.5mn, 4Q26E OP raised 13% to W856bn. GS says MLCC content doubles annually per AI GPU and FC-BGA substrate capacity additions are limited.
RoboTechnik: Buy, TP cut to Rmb732 from Rmb796, 2026-30E earnings cut 8-18% on longer optical equipment delivery times. 3Q26 gross margin beat at 49.0%; delayed shipments should lift 4Q26 revenue.

Hitachi: 2Q adjusted operating profit of ¥348.9bn beat estimates and guidance was raised. GS lifts FY3/27 onward adjusted OP forecasts 1%, keeps Buy and ¥6,600 TP, but expects the share price may stall near term on Middle East headwinds and a modest 40bp y/y DSS margin improvement. Lumada and HMAX are the re-rating catalysts.

Songfa Ceramics (as written in the report): 3Q26 record gross margin of 28.4% offset a 16% revenue miss, with net profit of Rmb3.1bn in line. TP raised to Rmb310 on a stronger margin outlook; 2028 earnings raised 3% to Rmb32bn. GS sees the revenue miss as temporary, from prioritizing Phase IV drydock capacity.

Hyundai Motor India: in-line 2Q, Buy, TP Rs2,460. Management expects 2H EBITDA margin to rise about 300bps versus 1H. The Bayon model targets 80k domestic units in year one and an EV launches in 4QFY27.
TVS Motor: 2Q revenue +44% and EBITDA +47% y/y beat consensus. FY27-29E EPS raised 1%/5%/10%, TP raised to Rs5,290. Board approved a demerger of the consumer finance unit.

Standard Chartered: Q3 PBT 13% above consensus on record wealth solutions, strong global markets and lower credit impairments. FY26 NII growth guidance raised to about 4% (c.$11.63bn) and FY26 ROTE to about 14%. TPs raised to 2,790p/HK$290; GS forecasts sit 3-4% above consensus.

Ping An Insurance: 3Q26 OPAT up 8% y/y and ahead of estimates, but life NBV fell 54% y/y, a large miss. GS raises FY26-28E OPAT 1-3%, cuts FY26E net profit 4% and FY26-28E NBV 5-6%, and lowers TP to HK$68/Rmb70. Buy.

New Oriental and East Buy 1QFY27: revenue momentum intact but margins weaker. Buy EDU with TPs cut to US$69/HK$54. Sell East Buy with TP raised to HK$17. Non-GAAP operating margin estimates cut 1.0-1.2pp for the group.
Iluka: Buy, TP cut to A$8.2. September-quarter mineral sands revenue of A$219mn beat GS by 9% on zircon and rutile volumes and resilient zircon pricing. Eneabba rare earth refinery is 65% complete.
Hindustan Unilever: 2QFY27 revenue +15% y/y with 7% volume growth, ahead of GS. Gross margin fell about 450bps y/y on input costs. TP cut to Rs2,325 from Rs2,450. Buy.

Wesfarmers: Sell, TP A$77 maintained. Bunnings sales growth is slowing, with recent weeks the weakest, and Kmart costs are higher from distribution center commissioning. Kmart sales are growing about 2.2% and Officeworks about 2.7%.

Syngene: 2Q27 miss with sales down 9% y/y and adjusted EBITDA margin 17.7%, driven by biologics destocking (gLibrela) and an estimated 11% CRO decline. FY27-29E EPS cut by up to 10%, Buy and Rs450 TP kept. Destocking expected to last one more quarter.
Hengrui: GS raises 2026-28E earnings 4.7%/1.0%/2.0% and 12m TP to Rmb76.3 after the 3Q call. Management expects a US$300mn Novo upfront payment. Buy.

Asia ex Japan FX/Rates: GS favors receiving KRW 2Y IRS expecting one more BoK hike to 3.25% (2026 Korea GDP forecast raised to 3.7%), long INR/IDR, short SGD/CNH, and long MYR/THB. Stops are tightened on all four trades.

Microsoft 1QFY27: revenue +19% in constant currency, adjusted EPS $4.89 vs $4.73 consensus, Azure +48%, cloud gross margin about 66%. Buy and $640 TP. Focus on Azure trajectory, 2027 capacity, custom silicon and ROIC on AI investment.

Alphabet Q3'26: GS expects an initial negative reaction. Search and Other revenue of $63.35bn and GAAP operating income of $40.58bn missed GS, with GAAP EPS of $2.12. Google Cloud revenue grew 103% y/y to $30.71bn and beat consensus. Capex of $51.4bn was below GS's $60bn forecast. Buy, $435 TP.

UK Banks: the Budget's temporary 3pp increase in the bank tax surcharge to 31% from January 2027 for 15 months implies a 1-2% 2027E net profit headwind for Barclays and about 4% for NatWest and Lloyds. This is below the 5pp the market feared. Barclays and Lloyds are Buy, NatWest Neutral.

Underlying NIMs expected to peak and plateau over 1H27, then decline in 2H27.
